pr_body:
Add a new devicetree.h API. This makes the current macros deprecated but keeps them around. The new API uses macros which are **not** generated, hiding the details of the generated macros from the user.

This is inspired by https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/22964#issuecomment-591785043 but "reverses" the capitalization: the names from devicetree remain lowercase. See the documentation changes for what I mean.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/22964
Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/22555
Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/22554

Per @galak and @pabigot:

Fixes: #21369
Fixes: #19285

TODO list:

- [x] fix documentation
- [x] pass CI (some linter checks must be ignored)
- [x] tests for all DT macros
- [x] list all the property suffixes in one place
- [x] cs-gpios helpers
- [x] finish fixing up howtos.rst
- [x] settle on an approach to phandles
- [x] reg and irq name macros
- [x] DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT
- [x] DT_NUM_REGS, DT_NUM_IRQS
- [x] generate a define for number instances ie DT_N_INST_<compat>_NUM
- [x] IRQ cell existence checks

Out of scope for this PR, to be addressed later:

- flash partitions

Starts of my initial cut at a naming convention that is consistent and has limited conflicts.

Thinking for things like DT_ALIAS, DT_IDENT, DT_NODELABEL would just be 'PATH' defines as such:

```

#define DT_NODELABEL_UART0 SOC_UART_4006D000
#define DT_INST_0_NXP_KINETIS_UART SOC_UART_4006D000
```

Than you can use macro magic to do something like:

``DT_ALIAS_PROP(UART0, LABEL) -> DT_PATH_P_SOC_UART_4006D000_LABEL``

Example of what we generate today for a register w/current PR from marti:

> I was hoping for something like this (draft status)
> <name> ::= 'DT_' <node-id> [ '_' <suffix> ];

As discussed in #22966, an ABNF for what we have now is here: https://github.com/mbolivar/zephyr/blob/doc-dt-improvements/doc/guides/dts/macros.bnf

This will hopefully be merged to master soon.

> Would have the following "path" prefixes (in the respective order they
> are defined in the DTS):
> 
>     * `DT_n_path_s_FOO_s_BAR_BAZ`
> 
>     * `DT_n_path_s_FOO_s_BAR_s_BAZ`
> 
>     * `DT_n_path_s_FOO_BAR_BAZ`

I went ahead and implemented some helper macros to make this style readable, and did the same for the other node identifiers. Examples are in the commit log for this patch:

https://github.com/mbolivar/zephyr/commit/019e18d5caad01549512065cc23135c77fc0aa4a

In particular:

```
Add helper macros which abstract the "true names" of each of the four
types of node identifier we intend to support:

- DT_ALIAS()
- DT_INST()
- DT_NODELABEL()
- DT_PATH()

Add a DT_PROP() macro which can be used to read the value of a
devicetree property given a node identifier from one of these four
other macros, and the uppercase-and-underscore name of the property.

Example macro expansions:

    DT_PROP(DT_ALIAS(UART0), CURRENT_SPEED)  ->
    DT_n_alias_UART0_p_CURRENT_SPEED

    DT_PROP(DT_INST(0, NORDIC_NRF_UART), CURRENT_SPEED) ->
    DT_n_inst_0_NORDIC_NRF_UART_p_CURRENT_SPEED

    DT_PROP(DT_NODELABEL(ARDUINO_SERIAL), CURRENT_SPEED) ->
    DT_n_nodelabel_ARDUINO_SERIAL_p_CURRENT_SPEED

    DT_PROP(DT_PATH(SOC, UART_40002000), CURRENT_SPEED) ->
    DT_n_path_sSOC_sUART_40002000_p_CURRENT_SPEED
```

As can be seen above, I think the basic form of a property macro can be `DT_n_NODEXYZ_p_PROPFOO`. We can keep the old macros around while we migrate to this new style.

I've looked at the other types of macros we currently generate and think this use of mixed case in the actual macros generated by scripts, along with helper macros that take arguments in devicetree.h to access them, is a workable and future-proof way forward.

One additional benefit is we can change the "true names" without big tree-wide problems as long as people use the helper API.

@erwango @mnkp @pabigot: I would like to discuss this approach tomorrow at the dev meeting. If it seems worth chasing, I will make the changes to gen_defines.py and handle the other special case macros as well.

We can use that to prepare to close this issue, along with #22554 and #22555. Of course we won't be able to really merge to topic-devicetree until @galak is back and can review, but it would be good to make progress meanwhile, and this proposal is along the same lines as his PR #22987.

Is this stuff that needs to be backwards compatible?

Otherwise, I think we should separate parts with two underscores. The macros we generate now are super hard to read (and pretty much unguessable if you don't already know how it works), since it's hard to see where parts start and end.

This is common in the Linux kernel too. Try this:

```sh
$ git grep '#define.*\w__'
```

Could have

```c
DT__ST_STM32_I2C_V2__40005C00__BASE_ADDRESS
DT__ST_STM32_SPI_FIFO__40003C00__CS_GPIOS__PIN
```

instead of

```c
DT_ST_STM32_I2C_V2_40005C00_BASE_ADDRESS
DT_ST_STM32_SPI_FIFO_40003C00_CS_GPIOS_PIN
```

for example.

Personally, that would've helped me enormously.

The generated header looks like this:

```
#define DT_N_INST_0_sifive_uart0 DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000

/* Generic property macros: */
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_reg {268513280 /* 0x10013000 */, 4096 /* 0x1000 */}
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_reg_EXISTS 1
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_interrupts {3 /* 0x3 */}
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_interrupts_EXISTS 1
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_clock_frequency 16000000
#define DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000_P_clock_frequency_EXISTS 1
... etc
```

So the macro expansion is roughly `DT_DRV_INST(0)` -> `DT_INST(0, DT_DRV_COMPAT)` -> `DT_INST(0, sifive_uart0)` -> `DT_N_INST_0_sifive_uart0` -> `DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000`.

The final token `DT_N_S_soc_S_serial_10013000` can get pasted onto `_P_clock_frequency` or something like that to get property values, etc.

So we're relying on being able to paste DT_DRV_COMPAT in the preprocessor, like `DT_N_INST_##inst##_##DT_DRV_COMPAT`, for this all to work. That means it has to be a C token.

So using "sifive,uart0" would require a solution where we could convert that string into that token at preprocessor time. I don't know how to do that.... any ideas?

> If not, I'd actually prefer the caps version. Adding a new, intermediate (with "_" but lower case) modified string is confusing IMHO.

> Reversing that so they are uppercase is possible, but would be a lot of work at this point. Is this a strong preference?

IMO this is a worse option because devicetree identifiers tend to be lowercase most of the time, so people just need to know to convert special characters to underscores in the C API.

We do need a consistent case in this naming scheme to avoid collisions. For example, uppercase `_P_` is used to separate the node identifier from the property name. Since the identifier and property names are lowercase, there is no ambiguity. If we don't do a case transformation, we can't be sure.

Please see macros.bnf for the details.
